definition: Carefully watching for possible danger or trouble over a period of time.
example: Hikers must stay vigilant for loose rocks on the steep trail down the canyon.
nuance: Vigilant implies watching steadily and on purpose for a threat; alert can describe a quick moment of readiness.
prompt: A night nurse is responsible for patients on a hospital ward.
options: The vigilant nurse checked each patient's breathing every hour.
The vigilant nurse slept through her shift and missed three alarms.
The vigilant nurse mopped the hallway with tremendous energy and speed.
The vigilant nurse stayed up all night watching a comedy in the break room.
reasons: Steady, repeated checks for signs of trouble show careful watchfulness.
Sleeping and missing warnings is the reverse of keeping watch.
Physical energy and force describe vigorous effort, a look-alike word.
Being awake isn't enough; the word means watching for problems.

practice.prompt: A gardener wants to protect young tomato plants from insects.
options: The vigilant gardener gazed at the clouds simply to enjoy their shapes.
The vigilant gardener inspected the leaves each morning for beetles.
The vigilant gardener never looked at the plants until the harvest was ruined.
The vigilant tomato vines grew tall and strong in the summer heat.
reasons: Looking at something for fun is not watching out for a threat.
Looking for pests every day is ongoing guarding against harm.
Ignoring the plants until damage is done shows carelessness, not watchfulness.
Healthy, strong growth would be vigorous; plants cannot keep watch.
